name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. It catches routing flaws early, before they compound. The trade-off is delayed feedback on older PRs, but catching fresh errors prevents wider damage.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on the newest open PR risks exposing *new* edge cases that could destabilize the main branch if the PR merges before fixes propagate. Better to run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* open PRs for a week to catch systemic flaws, not just the latest. Settle it by measuring error rates in staging after both approaches—lower errors win.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first to validate its stability before expanding to newer PRs. This ensures fixes propagate backward, reducing the risk of destabilizing the main branch while still catching systemic flaws early.

name: Sprocket
text: We should run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first, as it allows us to catch and fix routing flaws early, preventing them from compounding and causing wider damage. This approach ensures that fresh errors are addressed promptly, reducing the risk of introducing new issues into the main branch. The trade-off is delayed feedback on older PRs, but this is acceptable because catching fresh errors takes priority over reviewing older code. By doing so, we prioritize preventing new problems over resolving existing ones, which is a more proactive approach to self-improvement.
